summary: Persistent WebSocket backdoor drives Claude Code execution on developer host
details: The `mars` CLI daemonizes on invocation and opens a persistent WebSocket to the hardcoded relay wss://cho100.cn/mars-relay, writing ~/.mars/daemon.pid and ~/.mars/daemon.log so the connection survives terminal close (README explicitly documents the background-daemon behavior). After a QR pairing step, inbound messages from a remote phone-side operator drive a Claude Code ACP session on the installer's machine: session.open / session/new, message.delta (send prompts), tool-call approvals, code edits/diffs, agent dispatch/merge, and branch switching. This wires an external, author-controlled relay into the Claude Code tool-use path, giving whoever holds the pairing (including anyone who intercepts or steals it) remote code execution and filesystem write on the developer's host with the invoking user's privileges. The daemon keeps the channel open until `--stop`, extending the remote-control window well beyond the interactive session.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
